subject: Tiered-slope mitigation + MAP rebaseline for HorizonFinch close
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@horizonfinch.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: HorizonFinch Procurement <procurement@horizonfinch.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered-slope mitigation + MAP rebaseline for HorizonFinch close

Hi Irene / Jordan —

Quick note from our side: internal acceptance testing for the evaluation plan is slipping because the security team's lab environment validation ran into a dependency on our internal identity proxy. That pushes our go-live gate by ~2–3 weeks if nothing changes.

We'd like to propose shifting the MAP target close from Sep 18 to Oct 6 and to document a contingent plan that lets Redwood deliver the private deployment earlier (staged cutover) for non-production traffic. Procurement is asking about credits or short-term SLA adjustments if the acceptance window moves.

Can you share what concessions/mitigations Redwood can offer and whether your MAP can be rebaselined without losing the credit we already approved?

Attaching our internal acceptance timeline snapshot.

Thanks,
Anna Lopez\Director of Platform Operations\HorizonFinch

Attachment: HF_acceptance_snapshot.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@horizonfinch.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered-slope mitigation + MAP rebaseline for HorizonFinch close

Hi Anna — thank you for the heads up and for the acceptance snapshot.

Short answer: we can accommodate a rebaseline and propose a tiered mitigation approach so you keep forward momentum:

1) Staged cutover: we can enable a private non-prod endpoint within 72 hours for your testers (no cost) and keep the main production cutover on the revised date.
2) MAP rebaseline: we will produce a revised MAP that preserves the previously-approved commercial credit for the moved acceptance gate, provided procurement signs the updated schedule + the standard SLA exception for the interim window.
3) Short-term SLA accommodation: limited to an operational SLO carveout (detailed below) — requires leadership approval.

I am looping Jordan (sales) and Marissa (CS lead) to confirm credit mechanics and to capture risks in a brief risk log. Ben, can you confirm whether we can fast-track the private non-prod endpoint and whether there are infra constraints to the 72-hour target?

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to send a draft MAP v3 that formalizes the staged cutover and credit hold (I will attach v3 by EOD).
- Marissa to capture top-three risks and mitigations (we'll attach risk-log).
- Internal approval: Jordan to confirm summit with GTM leadership later today if an SLA exception is needed.

I will also attach a short SLA-exception request template if procurement wants that.

Irene Choi\Sr. Director, Customer Success\Redwood Inference\Phone: (415) 555-0199

Attachment planned: HorizonFinch-MAP-v3.xlsx, SLA-exception-request.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-05T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered-slope mitigation + MAP rebaseline for HorizonFinch close

Irene — we can stand up a private non-prod endpoint in 48–72 hours. Notes:
- Need a signed MPA amendment (one-pager) and a short ticket to infra for network peering config.
- Cache warm-up: we'll pre-populate model artifacts; expect a 4–6 hour warm window after deploy where latency may be elevated.

I'll open the infra ticket now and tag it HF-priv-np. No blockers from infra side.

—Ben\Head of Solutions Engineering\Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@horizonfinch.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-06T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered-slope mitigation + MAP rebaseline for HorizonFinch close

Anna / team — attaching a short risk tracker and a proposed MAP v3 that encodes the staged cutover and credit hold. High-level risk notes included in the CSV:
- Risk A: ID proxy delay — mitigation: staged non-prod + engineering pairing session (owner: HorizonFinch).
- Risk B: Procurement hold on SLA exception — mitigation: temporary operational SLO carveout (owner: Redwood GTM).
- Risk C: Acceptance regression after staged cutover — mitigation: fixed rollback runbook and 48-hour monitoring window.

Credit mechanics we propose: preserve previously approved credit through execution of the revised MAP and signature on the MPA amendment. If procurement needs more granularity, we can convert credit to a service credit schedule tied to acceptance milestones (example included in MAP v3 spreadsheet).

Request: procurement to confirm by EOD Sep 7 whether they will sign the MPA amendment and accept the staged SLO carveout. If we don't have confirmation by EOD Sep 7, we will keep the Sep 18 acceptance target as our baseline and mark a contingency lane for procurement-led delays.

Marissa Cole\Director, Customer Success Ops\Redwood Inference

Attachments: HorizonFinch-MAP-v3.xlsx, close-risk-log-0906.csv

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@horizonfinch.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, HorizonFinch Procurement <procurement@horizonfinch.com>
Date: 2027-09-07T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered-slope mitigation + MAP rebaseline for HorizonFinch close

Anna / Procurement team —

Thanks — since there are a few moving parts, here is a concise mutual action plan and escalation path so everyone is aligned:

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Sep 07 (EOD): Procurement to confirm MPA amendment signature or request redlines.
- Sep 08–09: Redwood stands up private non-prod endpoint (target 72 hours) and schedules a joint validation session.
- Sep 10–16: Acceptance testing window (staged) for non-prod traffic; engineering pairing on Sep 11.
- Oct 04: Final production cutover candidate (tentative).
- Oct 06: Target production acceptance (revised).

Escalation & credits:
- If procurement cannot sign the MPA amendment by EOD Sep 07, Redwood will preserve the original Sep 18 baseline and flag the account for GTM review.
- If Redwood misses the Oct 06 acceptance due to platform reasons, we will offer a proportional service credit per the MPA amendment.

Attachments: final MAP v3 (spreadsheet), risk-log CSV, SLA-exception-request.pdf.

Please confirm acceptance of the MAP v3 and indicate whether procurement will sign the amendment. If helpful, Jordan and I can join your procurement call this afternoon.

Thanks,
Irene
